headline: Lithium rebound lifts Albemarle back to profit, debt cut
summary_short: Albemarle posted Q1 2026 net sales of $1.43 billion (+32.7% y/y) and diluted EPS of $2.34, reversing a year-ago near-breakeven quarter on Energy Storage and Specialties pricing and volume gains. Adjusted EBITDA of $664 million (+148.5% y/y) accompanied a $1.3 billion debt paydown.
summary_long: Net sales rose 33% y/y to $1.43 billion on higher Energy Storage volumes (+14%) and pricing (+51%) plus Specialties gains; Ketjen's divestiture trimmed sales ~4%. Net income hit $319 million ($2.34 diluted EPS) despite a $95 million divestiture loss and $25.9 million of Kemerton Train 1 restructuring charges. Adjusted EBITDA rose 148% to $664 million on the same volume/price tailwinds plus cost actions. Operating cash flow fell to $346 million (Q1 2025 included a one-time $350 million prepayment); capex fell to $99 million, tracking the reaffirmed $550-600 million FY2026 range. The quarter's headline move: a $1.3 billion debt tender cut long-term debt to $1.88 billion. Management raised Specialties outlook and cut interest-expense guidance; capex guidance held.
